title: Sequence-length clustering for kernel routing and padding trimming
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Padding extremes in dynamic batching increase per-token cost and cause suboptimal kernel choices for mixed-length workloads. Current bucketing is coarse and static, leading to wasted compute on long padded sequences during prefill and decode. We need an adaptive, lightweight sequence-length clustering layer that informs kernel routing and trimming decisions at micro-batch time so we reduce padding without harming latency SLOs or KV cache correctness.

Objective: Implement a sequence-length clustering and routing component that: (1) forms compact buckets at request arrival time using a configurable clustering heuristic, (2) selects kernel variants (e.g., small-seq optimized vs long-seq optimized) per bucket, (3) applies conservative padding-trimming during prefill to minimize wasted tokens while preserving correctness for decode, and (4) integrates with existing fallback policies and metrics reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end e2e test demonstrates >=10% mean token-cost reduction for mixed-length workloads (seq len distribution: 8/32/128) while median end-to-end latency on P99-sensitive routes is within 5% of baseline.
2) Runtime exposes runtime knobs: clustering_strategy (kmeans-lite|quantile|fixed-buckets), max_buckets (1-16), padding_trim_threshold (0-0.5), kernel_routing_enabled (true/false).
3) Kernel routing defers to fallback kernel on incompatibility and records a metric trace that can attribute suboptimal routing.
4) No KV-cache correctness regressions (validated by decoder state replay test suite).
5) Feature gated behind flag and included in runtime-1.24 canary rollout with metric guards.
implementation_notes:
Design summary: lightweight online clustering at request queue boundary. We will implement two clustering heuristics: a quantile sketch that maps sequence lengths to buckets using P2 quantiles (low CPU), and a tiny kmeans-lite (k <= 12) seeded with power-of-two centroids for workloads that require tighter grouping. Buckets are represented as small metadata descriptors attached to micro-batches; kernel_router consults this descriptor to pick shader/kernel variants.

Kernel selection: introduce KernelVariant metadata (shortSeqOpt, longSeqOpt, tiledAttnOpt) and a selection policy that scores variants by expected throughput for bucket's representative length and active hardware (SM, memory). Score function will use offline profiler tables generated per model+hardware.

Padding trim: prefill code will compute per-bucket trim_point = floor(mean_len + padding_trim_threshold * stddev_len) and cap trimming to avoid OOM or KV-mismatch. Conservative trim for streaming/regen requests to maintain alignment.

Prefill/decode scheduling: scheduler will prefer to form micro-batches by bucket and schedule small-bucket batches on low-latency lanes; long buckets may be sent to throughput lanes. Implement preflight checks for latency SLOs and provide dynamic merge when underutilized.

Telemetry: emit tags bucket_id, bucket_repr_len, kernel_variant, trim_applied. Add perf counters for wasted_padded_tokens and routed_to_fallback.
testing_plan:
Unit: clusterer correctness on synthetic seqlen distributions; kernel routing decision matrix tests (including fallback).
Integration: run full prefill->decode flows with KV cache replay to ensure decoder integrity.
Perf: run CI perf harness with traffic mixes: short-only, long-only, mixed-8-32-128-512. Collect token-cost, latency histograms, and GPU utilization.
Chaos: simulate a sudden shift in seqlen distribution to validate dynamic bucket merge and safe fallback.
Canary: staged canary rollout on runtime-1.24 with metric thresholds (token-cost down >8% AND P99 latency not up >5%).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated merge to canary pool (5% traffic) - 2 days evaluation. 2) Expand to 25% with metric gating (token cost, P99 latency, failure rate) - 3 days. 3) Full rollout after 7 days if stable.
Rollback: disable flag and drain buckets; scheduler will revert to coarse static bucketing.
Monitoring: dashboard for token-cost, padded_tokens_saved, kernel_fallback_rate, kv-cache-mismatch-count.
comments: 2025-11-12: Spike results: quantile sketch + tiny-kmeans performs similarly on mixed traffic with <2ms CPU overhead per batch.
2025-11-20: Design review feedback from Priya: add explicit guard for streaming sessions (no aggressive trimming).
2025-11-24: Miguel: kernel routing hook implemented; awaiting perf CI and reviews; observed 12% token-cost reduction in local harness for the mixed profile.
